title: Add pane_send_key to the pane transport for herdr, tmux, and the test fakes
action: Add ONE method to `trait PaneTransport` (run.rs:434): `fn pane_send_key(&self, pane_id: &str, key: &str) -> Result<(), String>;` placed beside pane_close (run.rs:491). Implement it for RealHerdr (run.rs:633) as `self.call(&["pane", "send-keys", pane_id, key]).map(|_| ())` (herdr accepts `esc` as the canonical Escape name), for RealTmux (tmux.rs:462) as `send-keys -t <pane_id> <key>` WITHOUT the `-l` flag (a named key such as `Escape` must not be literal; see send_text_argv at pane_verbs.rs:311-318 which uses -l for text), and for every test double that implements PaneTransport: FakeHerdr (run.rs:3672), SharedLayoutHerdr (run.rs:3800), PanicHerdr (run.rs:4049), FakeCockpit (pane_verbs.rs:985). FakeHerdr and FakeCockpit record the (pane_id, key) calls in a Vec so hcc-4 tests can assert them; the others follow their existing style (SharedLayoutHerdr Ok, PanicHerdr panic). Do not touch CockpitTransport. Add one test per real transport that checks the argv shape (herdr: pane send-keys <id> esc; tmux: send-keys -t <id> Escape, no -l), following the existing argv-shape tests in pane_verbs.rs/tmux.rs. Run `cargo test -p bee herding::` scoped and the whole bee crate build must compile (every PaneTransport impl in the crate gains the method).

truths: Every PaneTransport impl compiles with pane_send_key
prohibitions: No second transport, no shelling out around PaneTransport
No change to pane_send_text or CockpitTransport
No behavior change to any existing verb
